writeup.headline: IQVIA rates Hold: strong momentum and raised guidance, offset by heavy debt and middling growth.
writeup.thesis: IQVIA scores 59, a Hold, 6 points short of Buy. The trend factor (91) is the main support: the price is 0.1% below its 52-week high and the shares are 69.0 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. News risk (71) helps too, after a Q3 beat, raised full-year 2026 guidance and a run of broker price-target increases. Quality is solid (64), with a 12.8% operating margin, a 12.0% FCF margin and the diluted share count down 2.7% year on year. Growth is only middling (49), with TTM revenue growth of 8.8% and growth slowed by 0.7 pp from the previous quarter. The weakest factor is the balance sheet (14): net debt is 6.56 times FCF and cash covers only 0.15 of debt. Valuation (52) is neutral: in absolute terms the FCF yield is 0.5 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield at 22.1x FCF and 26.9x EV/EBIT, and the multiples sit near the middle of their own history.
key_risks: High leverage: net debt at 6.56x FCF and a cash-to-debt ratio of 0.15 leave little cushion if cash flow weakens.
Growth is slowing slightly (down 0.7 pp quarter on quarter), and further deceleration would weigh on the growth score.
The shares sit 33.4% above their 200-day average and near their 52-week high, so a reversal could hit the trend score hard.
The FCF yield is 0.5 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, so in absolute terms the stock offers little valuation support if sentiment cools.
Regulatory and privacy matters, such as the recent Italian privacy fine, could resurface.
what_would_change: Up to Buy (6 points): faster revenue growth lifting the growth score from 49, or debt reduction improving the balance-sheet score from 14.
Up: delivering on the raised guidance and the roughly $9.4 billion of backlog expected to convert to revenue, with margins expanding.
Down to Sell (15 points away): a sharp drop in the trend score from 91 combined with negative guidance or analyst news.
Down: a further slowdown in growth or weaker free cash flow raising leverage.
